_note: Original advanced lesson. Shared across languages with language-specific code variants.
title: Sliding Window
summary: Track one **contiguous range** as it grows and shrinks.
refresher: A **sliding window** is the current range from left to right. As the right side grows, update the window **state**. When the window breaks a rule, move left and update the state again.
refresher_code:
left = 0
total = 0
for right in range(len(nums)):
    total += nums[right]

advanced-window-meaning.title: A window is a current slice
advanced-window-meaning.body: A **sliding window** is the group between left and right.
advanced-window-meaning.notice: The state must match the current slice.
advanced-window-meaning.mistake: Moving a **pointer** without updating the state **leaves** stale data.

advanced-window-shrink.title: Shrink when the rule breaks
advanced-window-shrink.body: Move left only when the current window is no longer valid.
advanced-window-shrink.notice: The while **loop** keeps shrinking until the rule is fixed.
advanced-window-shrink.mistake: Using if when you may need to remove several left **values** can leave the window invalid.

advanced-window-stale-state.title: Keep state honest
advanced-window-stale-state.body: If left moves, remove the old left **value** from your saved total or count.
advanced-window-stale-state.notice: The stored state should describe the real window.
advanced-window-stale-state.mistake: A stale total makes future choices wrong.

sections.title: What the window means
sections.summary: The window is one current slice.

blocks.body: A **sliding window** is a contiguous part of the **input**. Contiguous means the **values** sit next to each other with no gaps. The window usually starts small, grows on the right, and sometimes shrinks on the left.

blocks.title: Grow right, shrink left
blocks.caption: Watch a running sum stay matched to the current window.

steps.body: right moves to 0 and total becomes 2.

steps.title: Add 1
steps.body: The window grows to include 2 and 1.

steps.title: Add 4
steps.body: The total is now too large, so the rule is broken.

steps.title: Shrink left
steps.body: Subtract nums[left] and move left until the window is valid again.

blocks.title: Window vocabulary
items: left is the first **index** in the window.
right is the newest **index** added to the window.
**State** is the total, count, or table that describes the current window.
**Best** is the answer you have found so far.

blocks.prompt: What does the current window include?
blocks.why: The window is the current contiguous slice.

sections.title: Fixed-size windows
sections.summary: Some prompts tell you the window length upfront.

blocks.body: A **fixed-size window** keeps the same length after it is full. Add the new right value, remove the old left value, then compare or save the current result.

blocks.title: Slide a two-item window
blocks.caption: The window length stays at two, so one value enters and one value leaves.

steps.title: First full window
steps.body: Use 20 and 30 as the first two values.

steps.title: Remove left
steps.body: 20 leaves because the window must stay length two.

blocks.prompt: In a fixed-size window, what usually happens when a new right value enters?
blocks.why: The size stays fixed, so adding on the right means removing the value that just fell off the left.

sections.title: Grow right, shrink left
sections.summary: Update **state** every time the window changes.

blocks.body: Most sliding-window code has two movements. The right side moves to include a new **value**. The left side moves only when the current window breaks a rule. Each move must update the saved state.

blocks.caption: Longest subarray with sum at most limit, assuming nonnegative numbers.

python.code:
def longest_at_most(nums, limit):
    left = 0
    total = 0
    best = 0
    for right in range(len(nums)):
        total += nums[right]
        while total > limit:
            total -= nums[left]
            left += 1
        best = max(best, right - left + 1)
    return best

blocks.prompt: The window sum is too large. What should happen next?
choices: Remove from the left and move left
blocks.why: Shrinking from the left fixes the broken rule.

sections.title: Variable windows keep a rule true
sections.summary: Grow while useful, shrink when the rule breaks.

blocks.body: A **variable-size window** changes length. The right side tries to include more data. The left side moves until the saved state follows the prompt rule again.

blocks.title: Name the rule
blocks.body: Write the rule in plain words before coding: sum at most a limit, no repeated value, at most two absences, or a minimum total.

blocks.prompt: Why might a variable-size window use a while loop to shrink?
choices: One removal may not fix the rule
The right index is always wrong
blocks.why: If the window is still invalid after one removal, the left side needs to keep moving.

sections.title: Trace the state
sections.summary: The saved state must match the window.

blocks.caption: Keep the running total matched to the real window.
blocks.body: If left moves but total does not change, the code is now reasoning about the wrong window.

blocks.title: Sliding window needs the right kind of data
blocks.body: The sum example assumes nonnegative numbers. Negative numbers can make the grow-and-shrink rule unreliable.

blocks.prompt: Why is a stale total dangerous?
choices: The code makes decisions from an old window
It always makes the answer zero
blocks.why: The saved total must describe the same **values** that left and right describe.

blocks.title: See a stale total bug
blocks.caption: Watch the stored total become wrong when left moves but the old **value** is not subtracted.

steps.title: Window is too large
steps.body: The window [2, 1, 4] has total 7, over the limit 5.
steps.what_changed: The code must shrink from the left.

steps.title: Buggy move
steps.body: If left moves but total stays 7, the code is now lying to itself.
steps.what_changed: The real window is [1, 4], but the saved total still describes [2, 1, 4].

steps.title: Correct move
steps.what_changed: The saved total becomes 5, matching the real window [1, 4].

steps.title: Decide from honest state
steps.body: Now the next decision uses the actual current window.
steps.what_changed: **Sliding window** only works when the state and pointers describe the same slice.
